title: Your First Weekend at Seattle University, Shared as Cards
description: A low-pressure first-weekend loop through Seattle U’s First Hill campus, ending with a nearby free art stop. Confirm event and facility access before participating.

cards.title: Start by mapping your bearings
cards.subtitle: Self-guided campus tour • First Hill
cards.notes: Register for the self-guided option, then begin outside the Chapel of St. Ignatius and use the tour stops to orient yourself before making plans.
cards.short_summary: A structured first look at the campus with a clearly identified starting point.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s self-guided tour begins outside the Chapel of St. Ignatius and lets visitors explore campus independently.
cards.access_notes: Registration is required for this self-guided-tour option; follow the confirmation instructions.

cards.title: Pause at the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.subtitle: Campus chapel • First Hill
cards.notes: Take a quiet look at the colored-light interior during open visiting hours, or attend a listed liturgy if that fits your own interests and schedule.
cards.short_summary: A campus landmark designed by Steven Holl, with visitor and liturgy information posted by Seattle U.
cards.evidence_claim: The Chapel of St. Ignatius is Seattle University’s main chapel; its architecture uses colored light and it is open for visiting Monday through Friday.
cards.source_title: Architecture of the Chapel of St. Ignatius
cards.access_notes: The chapel lists visiting hours of 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Friday; it is closed Saturdays except for special events and opens around Sunday Masses.

cards.title: Meet up on The Green
cards.subtitle: Campus green space • First Hill
cards.notes: Use this named campus stop as an easy daylight meeting point, then consult the campus map together to choose your next destination without rushing.
cards.short_summary: A named green-space landmark on Seattle U’s First Hill campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s official First Hill campus map identifies The Green as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Use the official interactive map for current location and route details.

cards.entity_name: Lemieux Library and McGoldrick Learning Commons
cards.title: Find your library landing spot
cards.subtitle: Lemieux Library • First Hill
cards.notes: Walk through the library and learning commons, locate the service points you may need later, and save the building on your map for an easy return.
cards.short_summary: A map-listed library and learning-commons destination at the center of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s campus map identifies Lemieux Library and McGoldrick Learning Commons as a campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Some library spaces may require a Seattle University ID after hours; check library notices before visiting.

cards.title: Locate the Writing Center early
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Lemieux Library
cards.notes: Stop by the second floor of Lemieux to note the Writing Center’s location, then book a session when you have a draft, assignment, or idea to develop.
cards.short_summary: A student writing-support service located inside Lemieux Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s Writing Center is on the second floor of Lemieux Library and offers hour-long writing sessions.
cards.access_notes: The posted hours are Monday–Thursday 9 a.m.–8 p.m., Friday 9 a.m.–3 p.m., and Saturday 10 a.m.–1 p.m.; Sunday is closed.

cards.entity_name: Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center
cards.title: Get familiar with the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student Center • First Hill
cards.notes: Use the campus map to find the Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center, then check current listings there for student-facing events and services.
cards.short_summary: A named campus destination that appears on Seattle U’s official map.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University’s official campus map identifies the Student Center and LeRoux Conference Center.
cards.access_notes: Consult current building postings or university event listings for open activities and access.

cards.entity_name: Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center
cards.title: Scope out UREC
cards.subtitle: 14th and Cherry • South Campus
cards.notes: Walk over to the Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center, identify the entrance, and check UREC’s current facility rules before planning a workout or recreation visit.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s recreation facilities are located at 14th Avenue and Cherry Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University identifies the Redhawk Center and Eisiminger Fitness Center as UREC facilities located on 14th and Cherry.
cards.access_notes: Facility access and participation are subject to current UREC policies; verify before entering or working out.

cards.title: Walk by Seattle University Park
cards.subtitle: Athletics field • South Campus
cards.notes: Pass the field on a daylight campus walk and check the athletics or recreation schedule before assuming the turf is available for informal use.
cards.short_summary: A synthetic-turf campus field used for varsity athletics, UREC, and club sports.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University Park is a synthetic-turf field that accommodates varsity athletics, UREC, and club sports.
cards.source_title: Seattle University Grounds, Waste Management and Pest Control
cards.access_notes: Field use can be scheduled; view from public campus routes and confirm availability before any activity.

cards.title: Spot Logan Field on the south side
cards.subtitle: Varsity softball field • South Campus
cards.notes: Add Logan Field to your south-campus loop, then look for posted activity rather than entering a practice or competition area without permission.
cards.short_summary: A Seattle U field used year-round for softball training, practices, and competition.
cards.evidence_claim: Seattle University states that Logan Field Varsity Softball accommodates training, practices, and competition play year-round.
cards.source_title: Seattle University Grounds, Waste Management and Pest Control
cards.access_notes: This is an athletics facility; observe posted restrictions and scheduled activities.

cards.title: End the campus loop at Championship Field
cards.subtitle: Soccer field • South Campus
cards.notes: Find the field from the campus walk, then watch for a publicly listed game or event instead of relying on an assumed open-field schedule.
cards.short_summary: Seattle U’s natural-turf field and home venue for its soccer teams.
cards.evidence_claim: Championship Field is a Seattle University sports field that accommodates training, practices, and competition; Seattle U identifies it as home to its soccer teams.
cards.source_title: Championship Field Ready for Its Closeup
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled athletics and events; use Seattle U’s event listing for current public events.
